summary:
I've been building a character generator for SillyTavern that interviews you about a character, drafts a card, and can create it live in chat — the whole loop is Python-scripted end to end and pinned by tests that replay real model calls byte-for-byte, so a refactor either matches the recorded conversation or fails loudly.

The interesting part turned out to be lore, not writing. Every generated character ships background knowledge that's supposed to surface only when relevant — but on my hardware, anything that toggles in and out of the prompt forces the model to reprocess the entire conversation from scratch on the next turn instead of just the new line. I ended up pinning that lore as always-present instead of conditional. Costs a few hundred extra tokens per turn, buys back tens of seconds of dead air. Same fix, twice: I hit the identical problem with example dialogue in chat sessions, and made the same call — pay the token tax, keep the response snappy and the character on-model.

Adjacent to that, I built a "forge a persona" flow: instead of only generating the other character, you can generate the one you're playing — answer a short guided interview, get a face and backstory synthesized from it, one call, not a back-and-forth. Found a real bug in QA: a text field was wired up read-only by mistake, so the last question in the interview just silently froze the form. Small thing, but a good reminder that "the button didn't do anything" is often a one-line typo, not a logic problem.

Most of my week besides that was plumbing: getting a home automation agent to hold a conversation without losing track of context, and chasing why a browser microphone feature quietly stopped working — turned out the page was serving over HTTPS but making a request to a plain HTTP address, which browsers block outright and fail silently on. Not glamorous, but exactly the kind of bug that looks like "it's broken" and is actually "read the one log line that explains everything."

highlights.oneLiner: Getting a home automation agent to hold context across a conversation
